sentences.text: Now, we use only the original matrix.
Think of the matrix as layers.
For our 5 by 5 matrix, the outside border is the first layer.
Inside that, the 3 by 3 border is the second layer, and the center is left alone.
With the outer layer, the first four connected positions contain top, 1, right, 5, bottom, 25, left, 21.
For clockwise rotation, top must go to right, right must go to bottom, bottom must go to left, and left must go to top.
But we cannot write top into right first, because we would destroy the old right value.
Now move 21 from left into top, then move 25 from bottom into left, then move 5 from right into bottom.
And finally, move the save value, 1, into right.
The first four -position cycle is complete.
The four corners are now in their final rotated positions.
Move one position to the right along the top edge.
One final cycle for the outer layer.
Now the entire outer layer is complete.
Every value on this border is already in its final rotated position.
So we do not touch this layer again.
The inner layer is a 3 by 3 border.
Now the final four position cycle.
The inner layer is now complete.
The center value was never part of any four position cycle.
So it remained exactly where it started.
The entire matrix has now been rotated 90 degrees clockwise without creating another matrix.
The pattern is finish one four position cycle safely, continue across the layer, finish the complete layer, then move inward.
Now let's translate that exact movement into code.
